notes.title: The Marching Host
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 

Its' been a while! Hope you've been feeling great!

As you might know we've been beesy updating our other game, Bounty of One, for it's Daily Deal (it starts today, the 15th, at 7pm CET by the way). Check it out here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1968730/Bounty_of_One/

However, that doesn't mean that Hive Blight has been put aside in the meantime! Indeed, we've made a lot of change to this update and we have been hard at work advancing on new mechanics and the 3rd chapter.

First off, what we are adding to the game in this update:

Music-wise, we have updated the music for the Boss fight, they should now feel more epic than ever
We have added specific sounds to all insects, they will say things in a insectoid language when you draft them or place them on the board. This should give them more personnality and make them more unique. 
We'have change the fight background for Chapter 2 to be more ominous and make more thematic sens with the 3rd chapter we are working on. It is subtle but quite noticeable in game
Before:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/7241fc05e532bfe9a4b6b2b51a92607051f5d338.png
After: 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/6bcd4dc9a3f927216478aaf26d0759c2bbeacc99.png
We've added new enemies that will start appearing at the end of chapter 2. They each come with a specific mechanic and should give you a glimpse at what awaits you in chapter 3.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/44c357c0ea3062bb10dc0489666818b525c4c246.png
For those who have access to the Closed Beta: We have completely overhauled the poison system. It now deals damage equal to the stack amount of poison and reduce the stack by half every second. Therefore, we've rebalanced every units, items and trinkets linked to poison.


Secondly, what we're working on. At the moment, we are mainly working on two things: 

The 3rd chapter - we are working on finishing creating the 3rd and final chapter of the game: getting the vibe right, the enemies, the balancing and finally, the final boss. Here is a sneak peak of the 3rd chapter's background:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/c22944fc5789f6473a0739fe3fe4aaa126ddead9.png
The challenge system - we are working on specific map node where you can fight enemies while taking on an extra difficulty challenge in the hopes of getting something in exchange.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/f8df2aaabdaf97c547c43a6b9279f9a411414498.png


In addition to that, we've made balancing adjustments and quality of life improvement as usual:


Quality of Life:
Changed background battlefield of Chapter 2 to be more Blighted
Map improvement, 2 path with the same nodes should happen less often

Units:
New enemies with new mechanics for Chapter 2

Music and sound:
Boss fight now have updated fight music
Each insect now has a voice

Balancing:
Hector - base Attack Power buffed (T1: 10 -> 12, T2: 15 -> 18, T3: 20 -> 25)
Gustav - evolution rework, it now gives +0.1 Attack Speed with each evolution
Mothzart - evolution rework, it now gives +1 Attack Power with each evolution
Nikolai - evolution rework, it now gain one more Attack Power when it get heal with each evolution
Increased the difficulty of chapter 2
Spiky enemies now start with more spikes
Closed Beta: Poison Overhaul

notes.title: Post Steam Next Fest (mostly) Visual Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Steam Next Fest is now over, and we just wanted to say a massive THANK YOU to all of you who played the demo, wishlisted Hive Blight, or left a review, it means the world to us! Your support gives us the energy to keep pushing forward.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/03980d62e9e38405e45639c5c8828457ef4e25a9.png"]

Now, onto the actual update, both the demo and Beta have just been updated to match the current playtest version (if you don't know what I mean, go read the part "Want to try new stuff early?" at the bottom) ! But more fresh stuff is coming very soon...

Here’s what’s new in this version:

Quality of Life

 Enemies now reposition better during fights, reducing big enemy clusters and improving readability.

Balancing

 Mycelium Herald (Boss)
Old → “Invincible while elites are alive. Bloom: +1 Spike from Chubristle, +15 Chitin Grimhusk, and +3 Damage from Pale Apostle.”
New → “While elites are alive: Gains Invincible and Bloom: +1 Spike, +15 Chitin, and +3 Damage”
Attack speed: 1 → 0.7


 Big mushrooms should now appear a bit less often



Visuals


 New shop animation when buying items



FX Overhaul- New FX for:


 Enemy deaths


 Berserk activation


 Tempo triggers


 Poison-spreading trinkets


 Morgana’s area effect


 Heartbreaker effect


 Vignette when you're close to losing a fight

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/998db35b8a7d0408480d2dfb95c2d2284efc2b5b.png"]
Bug Fixes


 Fixed some UI buttons not showing correctly


 Fixed Blight Levels unlocking when they shouldn’t, or not unlocking when they should


 Fixed exploit with Rockamouflage and Ricin Infusion triggering during the setup phase



Testing Further Beyond


 Press ⬆️ during a run to unlock a very, very early version of Chapter 3. Curious? Go for it.



A few days ago (as some of you on Discord already know), we decided to slow down a bit when pushing new content to the main version. Just like we did for Bounty of One, we’ll now use a playtest branch to test features ahead of time, for both the demo and the main game! That way, we can make sure not to break our game when bringing new features to it!

Want to try new stuff early?


 Join our Discord: https://discord.gg/optizonion-games-915538608969101372


 Grab the “Entomologist” role in the #role-here channel

Enjoy, and thanks again for all the love!\

notes.content:
Hey everyone!


Big news first - Steam Next Fest starts today, and Hive Blight is part of it! 

If you want to help us gain visibility, the best thing you can do is play the demo, tell your friends, stream, make videos, or just spread the word in whatever way you can. It really makes a difference for us, thank you!

notes.title: Demo: Progression & Polish Update!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! 

For this first update of the demo, we bring you a mix of important progression changes, quality-of-life tweaks, and the usual balance and polish to keep Hive Blight smooth and shiny.

Let’s talk about the biggest change first.

Originally, our goal was to create a tutorial that didn’t feel like one. We’d drop players straight into a run, limit the mechanics to simple ones (like Heal and Spikes), and guide things gently through the quest system. The first boss marked the end of that intro, and behind the scenes, it helped ease players in without overwhelming them.

But it backfired. Many players thought beating that boss meant the end of the demo, and stopped playing—missing out on nearly 70% of the actual content.

So we’ve adjusted the flow:


 The first run is still simplified, but you can now go beyond the first boss and challenge Chapter 2 right away.
 Whether you win or lose your first run, you unlock the clan selection;
 You’ll also start earning experience and unlocking content immediately, right from the first run instead of starting progression beyond that point.
 Clan levels have been increased to 20 instand of 5


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/72a04889262f8ef2451b429c6e3e1888af570c59.gif

This should make progression feel more natural and help avoid confusion. Let us know how it feels!

Anyway, all this to say that if you've played the game and are reading this, you should probably give it another go cause you might have missed a bunch of content.

Outside of this main issue, here are the others changes we have made:
Fixes, balance & Improvements:

 Pebble Axe now inflicts 3 Shatter (was 2).
 Fixed Sharpened Shell not showing the Spike tooltip.
 Fixed Spike Elite not losing spikes correctly.
 Small visual improvements across the board.
 Changed Trinket and Equipment holders to look more distinct.
 New end screen when you leave the game — now featuring tiny insect devs!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/d4babdc8a67081fbd08efd73e7d4ebc805fa20bd.png
 Fixed Chapter 2 levels sometimes having too high difficulty.
 Changed end screen messaging so it doesn’t sound like “game over.”


Game System Updates:

 Removed the Introduction Chapter – you now start directly in Chapter 1.
 Clan levels increased to Level 20 (was 5).
 Units that leave your team are now returned to the draft pool.
 Blight Level unlocks are now visible in the Unlocks screen.


Let us know what you think of the new flow and all the tweaks. As always, your feedback is a big part of shaping Hive Blight!

Enjoy!

notes.title: The Hive Blight Demo is Here!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We’re super excited to finally share the Hive Blight demo with you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/4c98def001a5f0d5fbaadb693da3264ebbad1621.png

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3643400/Hive_Blight_Demo/

It’s been a wild ride getting here, and we couldn’t have done it without all your support. Whether you’ve been following the project for a while or you’re just discovering it now—Thank you!

This demo lets you step into the heart of the fight against the Blight. You’ll get to lead two very different but equally heroic clans. The Vespada are the kingdom’s main strike force: bulky, hard-hitting melee units that don’t care much for subtlety. The Sweet Symphoney, on the other hand, usually spend their time partying and playing music—but with the fungal threat spreading, they’ve come together to support the war effort with charm, healing, and proximity-based powers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/9925187ebce866a982627913b30dd4521fd1fc54.png

You’ll have access to 20 unique units, 20+ powerful trinkets and 20+ pieces of equipment, and get to fight through 2 full chapters filled with danger, choices, and cool synergies to discover. If you're feeling brave, you can also test your skills with 7 escalating Difficulty Levels for an extra challenge.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/a05ba0bcdb4e1c66f468dd9bad60adb2babf3c33.png

We’re still hard at work on Hive Blight, and we’d really love to hear what you think of the demo. Your feedback is super important to us—whether it’s bugs, balance, UI, or just vibes. If you want to share your thoughts or hang out with the team, come join us on Discord:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/12199fe63218497b575914bcb51ff91a7ffc8177.png

Right now, our top priority is reworking the map system to make runs feel more interactive and varied. You’ll already get a first taste of that in the demo when it’s done, and we’re planning to expand it even more in the future to keep each run fresh and unpredictable. But beyond that, we’d love to know what you think needs improvement—so don’t hold back!

If you enjoyed the demo, leaving a quick review helps us a ton. It boosts visibility, brings more players in, and keeps us motivated to push further.

And finally—huge thanks to everyone who helped us get to this point. Again, to all our regulars and everyone checking out the game for the first time: thank you. This adventure wouldn’t be possible without you.

Enjoy!

notes.title: The orchestral march!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Great news! Following our previous post, we have now added a new clan to the game:
The Sweet Symphoney!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/2784df5e4e371b1493f1eceee63929a749dc60c1.png

Usually, the Sweet Symphoney enjoy frivolous activities. They spend their time playing music, partying, and entertaining the other clans whenever possible. Faced with the fungal threat, they've come together to offer support to the war effort.

This new clan lets us double down on the clan system, and from our playtesting, each combination feels truly unique. For instance, with the Vespada limited to melee units, fights used to be very melee-focused. But with the Sweet Symphoney’s ranged units, there’s now a whole new way to approach battles.
Furthermore, this new clan comes with its own unique mechanics, trinkets and items. They focus on heals, crowd control (called "charm" here) and buffs. They may feel weak at first but, combined with other clans' abilities, they will allow you to make the fights last and eventually outscale your opponents.

Here are the new trinkets and items:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/4b1d1348892d2b17d79194fd3930e3c3edecbe5a.png

While I am at it, we would like to expand our tester base, if you want to give Hive Blight a try, give us your feedback and help us improve the game further, just head over to our Discord:

https://discord.gg/optizonion-games-915538608969101372

Once you’re there, grab the “Hive Blighter” role in the #roles channel to unlock the Hive Blight sections. You’ll then be able to request a key by sending us a message in the #request-key channel.



Here is a quick overview of their specific mechanics:

Harmony: Adjacent are affected by the listed effect.
Here's an example with ludwig:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/410291c28d00527e2c2fba7ae44f567aea06f906.png

Charmed: While a unit has some Charmed stacks, its damage is 0, each time the unit attacks it loses 1 Charmed stack.
Here's an example with Nina:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/c38463822f3696e9945d43b0a22e1f4b142276e9.png

Tempo: Triggers the listed effect every 4 attacks.
Here's an example with Gustav:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/ff41d237033a3012b311f8f4d5ceefe50d0f91a0.png

Heal: Heals the target by the specified amount (I know, unheard of)
Here's an example with... Bob: 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/3e6268a74df0e676f2cb18732cd01cd23b9d4217.png

Welcome back, bob!


We've also solved a few bugs, improved and fixed some UI elements as well as added many sounds for your enjoyment!

Anyway, that is all for today! Hope you like what you see!

Enjoy!

notes.title: A big change to unit design!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/6a62bc45d425b572a5eed3808d2b339f8c7eebd2.png

Hello everyone! 

It’s been a while, sorry bout’ that! But rest assured we were hard at work. Indeed, we have been rethinking the core balancing systems in Hive Blight, specifically the accessibility of each unit, trinket and equipment and it was no small task! In this post, I’ll go over the changes and why we’ve made it.

Originally, even though it made sense lorewise, we didn’t want to put the character you can choose from in specific factions. Indeed we wanted to avoid having a mechanic that gives you bonuses upon collecting multiple units of the same family, a mechanic which is often associated with factions in autobattler games. Instead, we thought it more interesting to give players access to a broad pool of units and mechanics—like poison, stealth, buffs, or lifesteal—and let them discover all kinds of wild combos.

This initial system had its merits, players could mix any units together and come up with unexpected strategies. This freedom also helped us during early development to experiment and see how different mechanics felt without the constraints of predefined clans. It further developed our understanding of our own game and made it easier to apprehend Units designs going further.
However, the system had flaws as well:

As we added new units and mechanics, the synergy for any specific mechanic—like poison—got harder to achieve. Too many diverse abilities meant you might never see enough poison items to actually build a cohesive poison strategy.
Each new addition risked making old mechanics too rare or creating overpowered interactions we hadn’t anticipated. Basically, any new addition could mean a rebalancing of all existing elements.


To resolve this issue, we thought of a different solution. We thought of giving players rerolls in order for them to have a chance to find the items or units they wanted. But as the pool grew, we’d have to keep expanding reroll options in order for players to hopefully get what they want. We felt like this wouldn’t feel satisfying as we want our player to engage in the mechanics of the game and make them work rather than get lucky. In the long run, this would never have achieved the right results.

We considered letting the game randomly “choose” a few mechanics each run (like poison + stealth + heal) to shrink the pool. But it felt convoluted and we didn’t want to force the player in a specific direction that they haven't specifically chosen themselves.

Eventually, we circled back on our idea to have clans - groups of characters sharing a theme and mechanics - but we knew that we still didn't quite like the usual “collect 3+ from the same tribe for a bonus.” It felt too straightforward and removed the joy of “outsmarting” the game by mixing unexpected elements from different factions. In the end we settled on a middle ground:
Limiting each run to two clans that the player chooses at the start.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/d4ae688f7e20950ec75e5aff2c4d3d2ac86a33fd.png

The Two-Clan System

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/9750f82292dea0ab0411a7a1a8137fdc671df6c7.png

Choosing two clans at the start accomplishes a few things. 

Firstly, clans and factions allow you to strongly define themes and mechanics for each of them and use known archetypes which, in turn, help guide the player towards the right strategies. For example, the first two clans we worked are staples of the genre:

 The Vespadas, the warrior clan. Heavy hitters with big health pools, high damage and little to no range option (think of your typical run of the mill warrior or barbarian). This clan includes the likes of wasps, hornets and other spiky insects.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/3382ef68acbf8a95eb4667411f6695d81d292dd0.png

 And the Silent Cabbale, the assassin clan. Smooth and nimble characters that focus on poison, stealth and lifesteal. Mantises, mosquitoes, flies are legions in this one.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/ea6cad26aaa7d20f4c2ee25ef3589ee71eaa3b00.png

Secondly, players still have a lot of agency in their choices. Because you’re combining two clans, you can still form clever synergies. Maybe mix the stealthy tricks of the Assassins with the brute force of the Warriors. Would you expect the poison from the Silent Cabbale to trigger the effects of some mechanics of the Vespada? Interesting!  We’re excited to see which combos players discover that we never even predicted.

Thirdly, the two-clan system makes balancing much smoother by keeping mechanics contained within specific factions.

Take our new Execution mechanic—effects that trigger when a unit lands a kill. We wanted to add a trinket, Moral Boost, which heals all allies by 2 HP when an Execution unit gets a kill. In the old system, this trinket would often be useless since Execution units were scattered in a massive pool.

Now, with clans, Execution-focused units are grouped together, ensuring mechanics like Moral Boost actually work as intended, leading to stronger, more reliable synergies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/e264dcfdb7acd236e1c643565f2e44bf85c6b754.png

Furthermore, this containment allows us to apprehend the combinations of the different mechanics more clearly and gives us room to make unique characters that have passives that might be just ok in association with some clans but shine brightly with others. For example, in our previous iterations, a character like Arilus, who gives his attack speed value to all allies upon dying, was problematic. Indeed, as it was fairly easy to build attack speed, he was good in almost any situation and was a “no brain pick” when you saw him in a unit draft. With the clan system, not only is he contained within a clan that we can balance on its own, even though he will always be good, he will only specifically shine in association with clan that have slow hitting units and/or good access to Attack Speed buff abilities. This way, it is back in the player's hands to figure out how good the unit is! Your new job will be to try out any combination of clans and find out how they interact with each other to uncover the perfect strategy!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/af87f5911e088740ccd27d260338fd25d3d5fae0.png

Challenges and Rework

All of this, however, wasn’t all sunshine - there were some big hurdles. Normally, we like to update the game on a regular basis so that we can have feedback on what we’re working on and advance alongside our audience. However, with such a big change, we had to shut down updates for a while as the games in its work-in-progress state would not be fun to interact with and feedback at that time might have been counterproductive because of it. Basically, the game was in a broken state for a while.

In addition to that, we had to reorganise and sometimes scrape a few existing designs (don’t worry, the overwhelming majority will make their comeback, they are just linked to other clans). We had about 25 units “tied” to five loose clans; some units could be repurposed with new clan-specific mechanics, but others had to go for now. That meant that in addition to repurposing some units, as we wanted each clan to have at least 10 units for replayability and variety purposes,  we had to create 5 to 6 new units per clan.
As we wanted clans to make sense visually and thematically, we also had to reorganise the way we handle mechanics so each of them feels distinct. Now, every clan has bound mechanics that only them (or mostly them) use and they might be limited on other fronts, the Vespada, for example, have no ranged units. Bounding mechanics to contain pools of units ended up being liberating however. Indeed, we used to be hesitant about adding certain gimmicks since it could end up useless in a random pool. Now we can design those mechanics confidently because each clan guarantees enough synergy within them each specificity to matter.

Anyway, thanks for reading so far (if you haven’t, thanks anyway)! We hope this explains why we pivoted from a single mega-pool to a two-clan system and how it keeps our game both balanced and creatively flexible. We’re excited to hear what you think, don’t hesitate to let us know!

Let us know your feedback. We’re always happy to hear from our community and see the inventive combos you come up with!


ps: Bob says hi!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/fbebab22c0d3d92ff24decfdc59349095a07ba0a.gif

notes.title: Welcome to Hive Blight!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We’re super excited to officially announce Hive Blight—our new roguelite auto-battler, where you lead an army of insect soldiers against the dark forces of a deadly fungomancer!

As of today, the game’s Steam page is live, and we couldn’t be happier to share it with all of you. Check it out, add it to your wishlist, and keep an eye on updates as we continue developing the game!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2886620/Hive_Blight/

We’re also looking for a few brave commanders to join the closed beta! 
Want to help shape the game, provide feedback, and get a sneak peek at what’s to come? Fill out the following form and let us know why you’d make a great beta tester. We're looking for players who enjoy auto-battler, roguelite, and deck-building games like TFT, Hearthstone Battlegrounds, or Slay the Spire, so if that’s you, we’d love to hear from you!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45211762/bbe6fa75a14ccae3f412fc6074f5c4bcbb1f6180.png

We’ll be selecting a limited number of testers to join us, so good luck, and thanks for your support!

Enjoy!
